statement: Given three distinct unit circles, each of which is tangent to the other two, find the radii of the circles which are tangent to all three circles.

Let \(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n\) be non-negative real numbers. Define \(M\) to be the sum of all products of pairs \(a_i a_j\) (\(i < j\)), i.e.,
\[M = a_1(a_2 + a_3 + \cdots + a_n) + a_2(a_3 + a_4 + \cdots + a_n) + \cdots + a_{n-1}a_n.\]
Prove that the square of at least one of the numbers \(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n\) does not exceed \(\dfrac{2M}{n(n-1)}\).

(a) Prove that \(10201\) is composite in all bases greater than \(2\).

(b) Prove that \(10101\) is composite in all bases.
Prove that the equation \(x^3 + 11^3 = y^3\) has no solution in positive integers \(x\) and \(y\).
Let \(a\) and \(b\) be distinct real numbers. Prove that there exist integers \(m\) and \(n\) such that \(am + bn < 0\) and \(bm + an > 0\).

(a) Prove that the values of \(x\) for which \(x = (x^2+1)/198\) lie between \(1/198\) and \(197.\overline{99494949}\).

(b) Use the result of part (a) to prove that \(\sqrt{2} < 1.41\overline{421356}\).

(c) Is it true that \(\sqrt{2} < 1.41421356\)?

During a certain election campaign, \(p\) different kinds of promises are made by the different political parties (\(p > 0\)). While several political parties may make the same promise, any two parties have at least one promise in common; no two parties have exactly the same set of promises. Prove that there are no more than \(2^{p-1}\) parties.

Four distinct lines \(L_1, L_2, L_3, L_4\) are given in the plane: \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) are respectively parallel to \(L_3\) and \(L_4\). Find the locus of a point moving so that the sum of its perpendicular distances from the four lines is constant.
What is the maximum number of terms in a geometric progression with common ratio greater than \(1\) whose entries all come from the set of integers between \(100\) and \(1000\) inclusive?
